items.title: In Yemen's Aden, divided government forces prepare for a Houthi assault
items.summary: ADEN, Nov 20 (Reuters) - As Yemen's Houthis push closer towards the temporary capital Aden against fragmented government forces, the city's inhabitants face a bleak choice: stay under fire or leave for an impoverished countryside. Aden has had no major warfare since bitter street battles of 2015, soon after the internationally recognised government fled Houthi-run Sanaa and made the port city its base, but it is now being hit by missile and drone strikes.

ai.sum: Houthi forces are advancing toward Aden, where fragmented government forces are preparing to defend the temporary capital.

items.title: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
items.summary: By Anthony Deutsch and Stephanie van den Berg THE HAGUE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The International Court of Justice's landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over the war in Gaza, legal experts said, establishing a precedent that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective. While the conflicts in Gaza and Myanmar are legally distinct, both cases before theWorld Court are based on…

ai.sum: The ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide is expected to strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over Gaza, legal experts said.

items.title: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh pledges ‘relentless diplomacy’ in bid to lead the UN
items.summary: Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati star diplomat running to succeed António Guterres, told Euronews the UN must return to its core purpose of peace, development, and prosperity. She has pledged relentless diplomacy, a leaner UN judged on results, and early action on wars from Ukraine to Gaza if chosen.

ai.sum: Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh, running for UN Secretary-General, pledged relentless diplomacy and early action on wars in Ukraine and Gaza.
